# Actual retained-cap facet limit and minimum-square moment density

This is a new ordinary dimension-reduction interface for PHYSICAL retained
volume. It is distinct from the projective-energy escort recursion. It
does not assert an OC inequality or identify a mixed-integer center.

Let K be a convex body in R^(d-1) times[0,infinity), d>=1, with a positive
facet F at height0. Fix x in relint F. Write

 T_K(y)=max{int_K f:0<=f<=1, int_K(w-y)f(w)dw=0}.

The proved ordinary hinge theorem gives

 T_K(y)=min_theta int_K[1+theta.(w-y)]_+ dw,

and its unique maximizing density is the indicator of one centroidal cap.
All notation for the normal dilation K_delta, fixed source Y=(x,1),
bounded tangential projection D, and local section convergence is as in
`candidate 1389446c1fac70ac`.
Those geometric facts use only convexity and the positive facet.

Define the finite-dimensional quadratic hinge functional on F by

 B_F(x)=min_a int_F[1+a.(z-x)]_+^2 dz.                    (1)

For a point facet use counting measure, the empty parameter, and B=1.

**Theorem.** The optimizer a_F in(1) exists and is unique. For the actual
compact body K and the normal inward approach y_delta=(x,delta),

 lim_(delta->0) T_K(y_delta)/delta=2 B_F(x).              (2)

In dilated coordinates the actual retained centroidal caps converge in
volume to the bounded cap of the infinite facet prism

 R={ (z,s):z in F, 0<=s<=2[1+a_F.(z-x)]_+ }.             (3)

The set in(3) is understood up to its zero-volume bottom points where
the affine expression is negative; the actual convex cap is
 (F times[0,infinity)) intersect {s<=2[1+a_F.(z-x)]}.
These versions agree up to d-volume zero. Their probability laws have
tangential marginal

 rho_F(z)=[1+a_F.(z-x)]_+/B_F(x),                        (4)

which is the unique probability density of mean x minimizing int rho^2
on F. Thus

 B_F(x)=1/min{int_F rho^2:rho>=0,int rho=1,int z rho=x}. (5)

The physical retained-cap limit is a quadratic moment minimizer. It is
not asserted to equal either the lower-dimensional retained mass T_F or
the projective energy E_F.

## 1. The quadratic hinge optimizer and its identities

Translate x to0. Suppose first m=d-1>=1. An inner ball r B_m in F gives

 int_F(1+a.z)_+^2 >= int_(r B_m)(a.z)_+^2=c_r |a|^2,

where c_r>0. Hence the continuous objective is coercive and attains its
minimum. It is strictly convex: for distinct a,b, both affine functions
are strictly positive in some neighborhood of0, differ off a hyperplane,
and the square is strictly convex there. Integration gives strictness.
Differentiation is legitimate by boundedness on compact F; the scalar
positive-part square is C1. With

 h(z)=[1+a_F.z]_+,

stationarity says int z h(z)dz=0. Pointwise h^2=(1+a_F.z)h, so

 int h^2=int h=B_F(x)>0.                                (6)

The strict positivity follows from the neighborhood of0 on which h>0.
Thus rho=h/B is a probability with mean0 and square integral1/B.

For any other probability density rho>=0 of mean0 (infinite square
integral is harmless),

 1=int (1+a_F.z)rho <= int h rho
                  <=(int h^2)^(1/2)(int rho^2)^(1/2).

This proves int rho^2>=1/B. Equality in Cauchy forces rho=h/B almost
everywhere, and that density attains equality. This proves(5), including
uniqueness, without an unproved infinite-dimensional KKT assertion.
For m=0 every displayed identity holds directly with h=B=rho=1.

## 2. Exact retained mass in the infinite prism

Let P=F times[0,infinity), marked at Y=(x,1). Its hinge integral for a
parameter(u,v) is

 G_P(u,v)=int_F int_0^infinity
                    [1+u.(z-x)+v(s-1)]_+ ds dz.         (7)

It is infinite for v>=0: near z=x its height-independent constant is
positive when v=0, and for v>0 the integrand eventually grows with s.
For v=-b<0, direct integration gives

 G_P(u,-b)=1/(2b) int_F[1+b+u.(z-x)]_+^2 dz
         =(1+b)^2/(2b) int_F[1+a.(z-x)]_+^2 dz,
 a=u/(1+b).                                            (8)

The scalar coefficient has unique minimum2 at b=1. Therefore the
unique finite minimizing parameter is

 (u_*,v_*)=(2a_F,-1),     min G_P=2B_F(x).              (9)

This minimum is the actual retained-mass optimum on P, even though P is
unbounded. The convex cap in(3) is bounded, has volume2 int h=2B, and
tangential centered moment2 int(z-x)h=0. Its normal first moment is
int(2h)^2/2=2B, so its normal centroid is1. Thus its indicator is feasible
and attains the mass2B. Every feasible density f with finite mass and
first moments satisfies

 int f=int[1+u_*.(z-x)+v_*(s-1)]f <= G_P(u_*,v_*).

This proves optimality directly. Pointwise equality gives its unique
indicator up to null sets. No general theorem for unbounded-body
optimization has been invoked.

## 3. Tightness and passage from the compact actual bodies

Normal dilation gives T_(K_delta)(Y)=T_K(y_delta)/delta by change of
variables, preserving the density ceiling and centroid constraint.
The fixed ball about Y contained in K_delta gives a UNIFORM coercivity
bound for every actual hinge objective:

 G_delta(theta)>=c |theta|,

by integration of the positive linear part over that fixed ball. The
single test theta=(0,-1) has hinge (2-s)_+, whose integral over K_delta
is bounded by2|D|. Hence every actual minimizing parameter theta_delta
is uniformly bounded. These compact bodies have unique noncentroid hinge
parameters for small delta: their ordinary centroid in original normal
coordinates has a fixed strictly positive height and so cannot be
y_delta when delta is sufficiently small. Alternatively any minimizing
parameters may be chosen, and the argument below identifies their limit.

Take a convergent subsequence theta_delta->(u,v). Almost-everywhere local
indicator convergence K_delta->F times[0,infinity) and Fatou give

 liminf G_delta(theta_delta)>=G_P(u,v).                 (10)

All integrands are nonnegative. The uniform upper bound excludes v>=0
by Section2, so the limiting normal coefficient is strictly negative.
Equations(8)--(9) then bound(10) below by2B.

Conversely test the FIXED prism optimizer(2a_F,-1) on K_delta. Its hinge
can be positive only for s<=2+2a_F.(z-x). Since z belongs to fixed compact
D, this gives a fixed finite height bound. On that bounded cylinder the
hinges are uniformly bounded and the body indicators converge almost
everywhere. Dominated convergence gives

 G_delta(2a_F,-1)->G_P(2a_F,-1)=2B.                     (11)

The actual minima are no larger. Equations(10)--(11) prove(2). Every
parameter cluster point must be the unique prism optimizer in(9), so
ALL actual parameters converge to(2a_F,-1). This proof keeps the actual
optimizers throughout and does not interchange an infimum and a limit.

## 4. Actual cap and marginal convergence

The actual maximizing cap in K_delta is

 R_delta=K_delta intersect
              {1+u_delta.(z-x)+v_delta(s-1)>=0}.

Since v_delta->-1 and u_delta is bounded, these caps lie in one bounded
height cylinder over D. Their indicators converge almost everywhere to
the indicator of the actual convex cap in(3). The exceptional set is
contained in the boundary of F and one affine hyperplane and is null.
Dominated convergence proves convergence in symmetric-difference volume,
and therefore L1 convergence of their normalized uniform densities.
Their first moments converge too by the same bounded support. Integrating
the limiting density over s gives h/B, exactly(4). Conditional on z,
the height is uniform on[0,2h(z)] and has mean h(z); its total mean is
int h^2/B=1 by(6). Undoing the normal dilation gives weak convergence
of the original cap laws onto that quadratic-minimizing facet density.

## 5. Exact interval-face calibration and scope

Let F=[0,1] and0<x<=1/3. Then

 a_F=-1/(2x),  h(z)=(3/2)(1-z/(3x))_+,
 int(z-x)h(z)dz=0,
 B_F(x)=9x/4,   2B_F(x)=9x/2.                          (12)

Stationarity and the strict convexity in Section1 certify the optimizer.
But T_F(x)=2x and E_F(x)=4x(1-x). Thus the physical retained-cap facet
coefficient9x/2 is neither2T_F(x) nor a universal multiple of E_F(x).
At x=1/2 one has a_F=0, B_F=1, and coefficient2, while T_F=E_F=1.
These are exact distinctions between the three ordinary invariants.

For any compact two-dimensional K with this bottom facet, the energy
limit is (27/8)E_F(x); the present theorem therefore also gives

 lim_delta E_K(x,delta)/T_K(x,delta)=3(1-x)
                                      for0<x<=1/3.     (13)

This is consistent with the strict sharp ordinary factor3 and approaches
it as the facet point itself approaches a vertex. The facet normal limit
is taken first at fixed x; no uniform edge limit has been assumed.

For d=1, F is a point and the theorem says T_K(delta)/delta->2, exactly
as follows from the interval formula2 min(delta,H-delta). The projective
energy instead has coefficient4. No lattice transformation, mixed-fiber
measure identity, critical-cap cover, or OC inference is part of this
ordinary theorem.
